title: Throwing an exception: refusing what cannot be

terminal.description: A shell in your workspace. Run the booking desk here, and try your classes from main.

tasks.title: Refuse an age that cannot be
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 1`, write a class `Fares` with a method `static int fareFor(int age)`. It gives back `160` for an age under 16 and `320` for 16 and over. An age below 0 is refused: it throws an `IllegalArgumentException` whose message names the age.

Check calls `fareFor` with ages of its own, 0, 15 and 16 included, and with ages below 0. It reads what comes back, and for an age below 0 which exception reached it and whether its message names the age.
nextSteps: Read the part of the lesson about throw.
Write the class and fareFor, with the two fares, as in earlier issues.
Before the fares, refuse an age below 0, with a message that names it.
Take the // off the first line in main, and try an age below 0 too.
hints: The refusal goes first: once the method has given back a fare, it is too late.
throw ends the method and hands the exception to the caller. The exception is made with new, and its message is joined from words and the age.
The first lines: `if (age < 0) { throw new IllegalArgumentException("No fare for an age of " + age); }`.

tasks.title: Refuse a booking before it changes anything
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 2`, write a class `Sailing` with a constructor `Sailing(int seats)`, a method `int free()` that gives back the seats still free, and a method `boolean book(int places)`. Fewer than 1 place is refused: `book` throws an `IllegalArgumentException` whose message names the places, and changes nothing. More places than are free is an answer, not a mistake: `book` gives back `false` and changes nothing. Otherwise it books the places and gives back `true`.

Check makes sailings of its own, two at once included, books them, asks for too many and for 0 or fewer places, and reads what `book` gives back, which exception reached it, and how many seats are free afterwards.
nextSteps: Read the parts of the lesson about refusing first, and about giving back an answer or throwing.
Write the field, the constructor and free().
In book, refuse fewer than 1 place before anything else.
Then give back false for a full boat, or book and give back true.
hints: A full boat is something the caller expects and can deal with; 0 places is a mistake in the code that asked.
The order matters: refuse, then check for room, and change the seats free only on the last line before giving back true.
The first lines of book: `if (places < 1) { throw new IllegalArgumentException("Cannot book " + places + " places"); }`, then `if (places > free) { return false; }`.

tasks.title: Say a crossing is cancelled, and say it on the notice
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 3`, write a class `Crossings` with two methods.

`static String board(int hour, boolean gale)` gives back `Boarding the 14:00 crossing`, with its hour. An hour below 0 or above 23 is refused with an `IllegalArgumentException` whose message names the hour, whatever the weather. In a gale it throws a `CancelledException`, given above the tasks, whose message names the crossing, as in `14:00`.

`static String notice(int hour, boolean gale)` gives back what `board` gives back, or, when the crossing is cancelled, `Cancelled: ` and the exception's message. A caller of `notice` needs no `try`, and an hour that cannot be still reaches its caller.

Check calls both with hours of its own, in calm and in a gale. It also compiles lines of its own: a call of `board` with no `try`, which must be refused because `CancelledException` is checked, a `catch` of `CancelledException` around `board`, and a call of `notice` with no `try`, which must be accepted.
nextSteps: Read the part of the lesson about checked and unchecked exceptions.
Write board: refuse the hour first, then throw a CancelledException in a gale, then give back the boarding line.
Run the file and read what the compiler says about board, then fix its first line.
Write notice with a catch for the one exception a gale brings.
hints: CancelledException extends Exception, so it is checked: the compiler wants every method that may throw it to say so, and every caller to catch it or say so too.
board names CancelledException after throws on its first line; notice catches it, so notice needs no throws. IllegalArgumentException is unchecked and goes on to the caller of notice by itself.

The first line of board: `static String board(int hour, boolean gale) throws CancelledException {`; notice is `try { return board(hour, gale); } catch (CancelledException e) { return "Cancelled: " + e.getMessage(); }`.
